cases.translation: November was already standing at the gate
cases.explain: Ноябрь is the grammatical subject of стоял (was standing), so it takes the nominative case.

cases.sentence: Люблю я дружеские враки и дружеский бокал ___
cases.translation: I love friendly chatter and a friendly glass of wine
cases.explain: Бокал (a glass of) governs the genitive of content, so вино becomes вина.

cases.sentence: И отправлялся налегке к бегущей под горы ___
cases.translation: And he would set off lightly to the river running below the hill
cases.explain: The preposition к (toward) always requires the dative case, so река becomes реке.
Руку is the direct object of the transitive verb подал (offered), so it takes the accusative case.

cases.translation: I hand myself over to your judgment
cases.explain: The preposition на with a verb of submitting (отдаю) governs the accusative here, so суд stays суд.
The verb жил (lived) takes an instrumental predicate to express 'lived as,' so анахорет becomes анахоретом.

cases.translation: The table is laid in front of the fireplace
cases.explain: The preposition перед (in front of) governs the instrumental case, so камин becomes камином.

cases.translation: She grieves over her unworthy husband
cases.explain: The preposition о (about) governs the prepositional case, so муж becomes муже.

reading.ru: Чем меньше женщину мы любим, тем легче нравимся мы ей, и тем ее вернее губим среди обольстительных сетей.
reading.question: What cynical observation opens this chapter about love?
options: The less we love a woman, the easier we please her and the more surely we ruin her
The more we love a woman, the happier she becomes
Women never fall for such tactics
reading.correct: The less we love a woman, the easier we please her and the more surely we ruin her
reading.explain: The chapter opens with this cynical maxim about love and seduction.

reading.ru: Так точно думал мой Евгений.
reading.question: Whose cynical views on love does the narrator say match the opening maxim?
reading.correct: Evgeny's (Onegin's)
reading.explain: The narrator confirms 'that is exactly what my Evgeny thought,' linking Onegin to the cynical opening.

reading.ru: Вот как убил он восемь лет, утратя жизни лучший цвет.
reading.question: How does the narrator summarize Onegin's past eight years?
options: He killed/wasted eight years, losing the best bloom of his life
He spent eight years studying abroad
He spent eight years happily married
He spent eight years serving in the army
reading.correct: He killed/wasted eight years, losing the best bloom of his life
reading.explain: The text says 'this is how he killed eight years, losing life's best bloom.'

reading.ru: Но, получив послание Тани, Онегин живо тронут был.
reading.question: How did Onegin react to receiving Tatiana's letter?
reading.correct: He was genuinely moved
reading.explain: The text states that on receiving Tanya's letter, 'Onegin was keenly touched.'

reading.ru: Теперь мы в сад перелетим, Где встретилась Татьяна с ним.
reading.question: Where does the narrator take us to witness the encounter between Onegin and Tatiana?
reading.correct: Into the garden
reading.explain: The narrator says 'now let us fly into the garden, where Tatiana met him.'

reading.ru: Мне ваша искренность мила
reading.question: What does Onegin tell Tatiana about her letter's sincerity?
options: That her sincerity is dear/pleasing to him
reading.correct: That her sincerity is dear/pleasing to him
reading.explain: Onegin tells her, 'your sincerity is dear to me,' before delivering his rebuff.

reading.ru: Но я не создан для блаженства, ему чужда душа моя.
reading.question: What does Onegin claim about his own capacity for happiness?
options: That he was not made for bliss, that his soul is foreign to it
That he has never experienced sadness
That he is destined for great happiness
That only Tatiana could make him happy
reading.correct: That he was not made for bliss, that his soul is foreign to it
reading.explain: Onegin tells Tatiana plainly, 'I was not created for bliss, my soul is foreign to it.'

reading.ru: Начнете плакать, ваши слезы не тронут сердце моего, а будут лишь бесить его.
reading.question: What does Onegin predict would happen if Tatiana cried in a marriage to him?
options: Her tears would not move his heart, only irritate it
Her tears would soften him instantly
He would cry along with her
He would leave the house immediately
reading.correct: Her tears would not move his heart, only irritate it
reading.explain: Onegin warns that her tears 'will not touch my heart, but will only irritate it.'

reading.ru: Мечтам и годам нет возврата, не обновлю души моей.
reading.question: What does Onegin say about his dreams and years, and his soul?
options: There is no return to dreams and years past, he will not renew his soul
He plans to start his life completely over
He believes dreams always come true eventually
His soul has already been renewed by love
reading.correct: There is no return to dreams and years past, he will not renew his soul
reading.explain: Onegin says 'there is no return to dreams and years, I will not renew my soul.'

reading.ru: Я вас люблю, любовью брата, и, может быть, еще нежней.
reading.question: How does Onegin describe the kind of love he feels for Tatiana?
options: Like a brother's love, and perhaps even more tender
No love at all, only pity
A love he intends to act on immediately
reading.correct: Like a brother's love, and perhaps even more tender
reading.explain: Onegin tells her, 'I love you with a brother's love, and perhaps even more tenderly.'

reading.ru: Он подал руку ей.
reading.question: What gesture does Onegin make to Tatiana after his speech?
options: He turns away and leaves without a word
reading.correct: He offers her his hand/arm
reading.explain: The text says simply, 'He offered her his hand,' as they walked back.

reading.ru: Увы, Татьяна увядает, бледнеет, гаснет и молчит.
reading.question: How does Tatiana change after Onegin's rejection?
options: She withers, grows pale, fades, and falls silent
She immediately falls ill with a fever
She leaves the countryside for Moscow
reading.correct: She withers, grows pale, fades, and falls silent
reading.explain: The narrator laments that 'Tatiana withers, grows pale, fades, and is silent.'

reading.ru: Час от часу плененной боли красами Ольги молодой Владимир сладостной неволе предался полную душой.
reading.question: How does Lensky's feeling for Olga develop, hour by hour?
options: He surrenders his whole soul to a sweet captivity, ever more enchanted by young Olga's charms
He grows steadily colder toward her
He begins to prefer Tatiana instead
He decides to end the relationship
reading.correct: He surrenders his whole soul to a sweet captivity, ever more enchanted by young Olga's charms
reading.explain: The text says hour by hour, captivated by young Olga's charms, Vladimir surrendered his whole soul to sweet captivity.

reading.ru: Они в саду рука с рукой, гуляют утренней порой.
reading.question: How do Lensky and Olga spend their mornings?
options: Walking hand in hand in the garden
reading.correct: Walking hand in hand in the garden
reading.explain: The text describes them walking 'hand in hand' in the garden during the morning hour.

reading.ru: Он иногда читает Оле Нравоучительный роман
reading.question: What does Lensky sometimes read aloud to Olga?
reading.correct: A morally instructive novel
reading.explain: The text says 'he sometimes reads to Olya a morally instructive novel.'

reading.ru: Уединясь от всех далеко, Они над шахматной доской На стол облокотясь порою сидят, Задумавшись глубоко.
reading.question: What quiet activity do Lensky and Olga share, sitting deep in thought?
options: Playing chess, leaning on the table
reading.correct: Playing chess, leaning on the table
reading.explain: The text describes them secluded together, leaning over a chessboard, deep in thought.

reading.ru: Владимир и писал бы оды, да Ольга не читала их.
reading.question: Why, according to the narrator, doesn't Lensky write odes instead of elegies?
options: Because Olga did not read them
Because he had no talent for odes
Because odes were forbidden by the censor
reading.correct: Because Olga did not read them
reading.explain: The narrator jokes that Vladimir would have written odes too, 'but Olga did not read them.'

reading.ru: а что ж онегин кстати братья терпенья вашего прошу его вседневные занятия я вам подробно опишу
reading.question: What does the narrator promise to describe in detail about Onegin?
reading.correct: Onegin's everyday activities/routine
reading.explain: The narrator asks the reader's patience, promising to describe Onegin's 'everyday occupations' in detail.

reading.ru: онегин жил анахаретом
reading.question: How is Onegin's lifestyle in the countryside described?
reading.correct: Like a hermit
reading.explain: The text says 'Onegin lived like a hermit (anachoret),' isolated in the country.

reading.ru: Стоял ноябрь уж у двора.
reading.question: What month has arrived as the seasons turn in this chapter?
reading.correct: November
reading.explain: The text states plainly, 'November already stood at the gate.'

reading.ru: Читатель ждет у шрифмы розы. На, вот, возьми ее скорей.
reading.question: What playful, self-aware remark does the narrator make about rhyme?
options: He jokes that the reader is waiting for the rhyme 'rose' and hands it over
He apologizes for having no rhymes at all
He claims he never uses flower imagery
He asks the reader to supply their own rhyme
reading.correct: He jokes that the reader is waiting for the rhyme 'rose' and hands it over
reading.explain: The narrator teases that the reader awaits the rhyme 'rose' (розы) and playfully supplies it at once.

reading.ru: Прямым Онегин Чильдгарольдом Вдался в задумчивую лень.
reading.question: To which famous Byronic literary character is Onegin compared here?
reading.correct: Childe Harold
reading.explain: The text compares Onegin directly to 'Childe Harold,' sunk into pensive idleness.

reading.ru: Настанет вечер деревенский, Бильярд оставлен, кий забыт, Перед камином стол накрыт, Евгений ждет.
reading.question: What happens each evening as Lensky is expected to visit Onegin?
options: Billiards is set aside and a table is laid before the fireplace
reading.correct: Billiards is set aside and a table is laid before the fireplace
reading.explain: The text describes the country evening when billiards is abandoned and the table is set before the fireplace as Evgeny waits.

reading.ru: Мой бедный Ленский, сердцем он, для жизни он и был рожден.
reading.question: How does the narrator characterize Lensky's fundamental nature near the chapter's end?
options: He was born for life itself, being a man of the heart
He was born to be a soldier
He was born to be a cold cynic like Onegin
He was born to inherit a fortune
reading.correct: He was born for life itself, being a man of the heart
reading.explain: The narrator calls him 'my poor Lensky,' a man of the heart, 'born for life' itself.

reading.ru: Он был любим, по крайней мере, так думал он, и был счастлив.
reading.question: What did Lensky believe about Olga's feelings, making him happy?
options: He believed he was loved, and so he was happy
He believed she had betrayed him
He believed she loved Onegin instead
He believed she was leaving for the city
reading.correct: He believed he was loved, and so he was happy
reading.explain: The text says 'he was loved, at least so he thought, and was happy.'
